relatedEntities.name: Thymol / mint oil fractions
relatedEntities.notes: Natural isolation vs synthetic hydrogenation routes

properties.appearance: Colorless crystals with characteristic mint odor
properties.solubility: Slightly soluble in water; freely soluble in alcohols and oils

hazards.notes: Terpene hydrogenation and isomerization catalysts, plus flammable solvents/terpenes, drive plant EHS.

overview: (-)-Menthol is obtained from natural mint oils (crystallization) and by synthetic / semi-synthetic industrial routes, notably Takasago’s asymmetric isomerization–hydrogenation sequence from myrcene. This dossier outlines both natural isolation logic and the modern catalytic industrial route for plant planning.
manufacturingSummary: Natural: fractional crystallization of dementholized mint oil. Synthetic: multi-step catalytic sequence from petrochemical or renewable terpenes with enantioselective steps for (-)-isomer.

environmentBaseline.notes: Low melting solid: handle molten transfers carefully to avoid solidification in lines.

ehsHighlights: Terpene flammability and peroxide formation risk on storage

routes.name: Takasago-type catalytic asymmetric route (industrial synthetic)
routes.summary: Myrcene-derived allylic amine undergoes asymmetric isomerization (Rh-BINAP class catalysts historically) to enamine/aldehyde intermediates, followed by cyclization and hydrogenation steps to (-)-menthol. Exact step packages are proprietary; patents and reviews provide the industrial narrative.

materials.name: Rh-chiral phosphine isomerization catalyst (class)
materials.notes: Historical BINAP systems; modern variants exist

steps.title: Feed preparation and allylic amine formation
steps.description: Convert myrcene feed to diethylgeranylamine (or process equivalent) via catalytic addition chemistry per industrial package.
steps.mechanismNotes: Sets the allylic amine substrate for asymmetric isomerization. Feed purity affects catalyst life.

steps.title: Asymmetric isomerization
steps.description: Isomerize allylic amine with chiral Rh catalyst to the enantioenriched enamine; hydrolyze to citronellal-type intermediate as applicable.
steps.mechanismNotes: Classic demonstration of industrial enantioselective catalysis: chiral ligand environment differentiates enantiomeric pathways, delivering high ee citronellal precursors after workup.
steps.scaleNotes: Oxygen and poison control for Rh catalysts is non-negotiable at all scales.

steps.title: Cyclization and hydrogenation to menthol
steps.description: Acid-catalyzed cyclization (e.g. to isopulegol) and stereoselective hydrogenation yield menthol isomers; purify (-)-menthol by distillation and crystallization.
steps.mechanismNotes: Citronellal → isopulegol type cyclization followed by C=C hydrogenation. Diastereomer control and crystallization upgrade optical purity.

routes.isolation: Fractional distillation and crystallization; handle as low-melting solid.

scaleUp.pilotToCommercial: Catalyst recycle loops and continuous hydrogenation improve economics.
scaleUp.safetyScaleUp: H2 systems, terpene peroxide management, molten solid transfer design.
scaleUp.greenChemistryNotes: Asymmetric catalysis reduces waste vs classical resolution of racemic menthol.

routes.name: Natural mint oil crystallization
routes.summary: Freeze-crystallize menthol from dementholized cornmint or peppermint oils; centrifuge and recrystallize.

steps.title: Chill crystallization and isolation
steps.description: Cool oil to crystallize menthol; centrifuge; wash and recrystallize to grade. Mother liquor is dementholized oil co-product.
